description: PARTIAL derivation of the p-n flavor split. Proves the subleading correction is SECOND-ORDER in the proven leading split (α·leading², from a multiplicative quark-pair factorization M ~ ∏(1+δ_pair) whose cross-term is O(leading²)), NOT a fixed ℏ_q-power. Derives what the pair-count structure predicts for the coefficient (bracketed in (⅓,1]; geometric self-energy reading = 1, within 7.6% of the experimental α≈0.929) and compares to 0.929 WITHOUT fitting. Evaluated at proton- and muon-anchored q₀. Single open piece: the exact self-energy normalization α. NOT production-wired. See docs/audits/2026-06-29-flavor-split-partial-derivation.md.

part1_second_order_evidence.note: Only the `leading` base gives an O(1) coefficient (≈0.929). Every fixed ℏ_q-power needs a non-O(1) fudge (ℏ_q³ → 1.31, ℏ_q² → 0.10-scale, etc.), the signature of a wrong shape. The correction SCALES with leading ⇒ it is α·leading² overall.

part1c_corpus_interface_product.note: The corpus interface factor f_pn = z·(1+δ_eff) is genuinely multiplicative; a product of two expands to 2δ_eff + δ_eff², confirming O(δ²) cross-terms are a REAL feature of the closed_form_tau_M interface product, not a probe artifact. (This is the INTER-nucleon interface; the flavor split is the INTRA-nucleon 3-pair analogue — same multiplicative algebra.)

part2_coefficient_prediction.reading_a_note: (m−1)/(2m) ≤ ½ for any m ⇒ a SYMMETRIC equal-split cross-pair count cannot reach 0.929. The pairs are NOT equally weighted; the swapped pair dominates.
part2_coefficient_prediction.reading_b_note: The full self-energy reading predicts coefficient EXACTLY 1 (parameter-free, the correction scale IS the leading split). It OVERSHOOTS 0.929 by 7.6%, giving 0.0097-0.0099% vs CODATA — 13× better than leading. This is the closest principled prediction.
part2_coefficient_prediction.honest_verdict: The structure forces the SECOND-ORDER form and predicts α = O(1), bracketed strictly in (⅓, 1]. The geometric self-energy reading (α=1) is within 7.6%. NO principled count lands exactly on 0.929 — that exact coefficient (the self-energy NORMALIZATION) is the single remaining OPEN piece. Per anti-flip-flop discipline the probe does NOT fit 0.929 to a clean form.

verdict.rigorously_established: (1) The subleading correction is SECOND-ORDER in the proven leading split — form α·leading² — NOT a fixed ℏ_q-power. PROOF: (a) no fixed ℏ_q^k base gives an O(1) coefficient for C_true−1 (every power needs a non-O(1) fudge), whereas `leading` gives α≈0.93=O(1); (b) a multiplicative pair product ∏(1+s_k) with Σs_k=leading has cross-term Σ_{k<l}s_k s_l = O(leading²) by pure algebra; (c) the corpus closed_form_tau_M interface factor f_pn=z·(1+δ_eff) is genuinely multiplicative, so O(δ²) cross-terms are a REAL corpus feature. The sign is POSITIVE (C_true>1) and the magnitude O(leading²)≈1.9e-6 matches the needed correction C_true−1≈1.3e-3 ⟹ coefficient O(1).
verdict.coefficient_predicted_by_structure: The pair structure BRACKETS the coefficient: symmetric equal-split cross-pair count gives (m−1)/(2m) ≤ ½ (undershoots); full self-energy/geometric reading gives EXACTLY 1 (parameter-free, overshoots by 7.6%). The experimental α=(C_true−1)/leading ≈ 0.929 sits in (⅓, 1], closest to the self-energy reading (within 7.6%). 13/14=0.9286 is numerically near 0.929 but does NOT fall out of the pair count and is NOT adopted (anti-flip-flop).
verdict.single_open_piece: The EXACT second-order normalization coefficient α ≈ 0.929. The structure proves 0 < α ≤ 1 and predicts O(1); it does not yet pin 0.929. Closing this is the self-energy normalization of the 3-strand spectator coupling — open Archimedean-mass-functor R&D, the same level that gates Δ_λ. α also DEPENDS ON C_DATA (experimental), so it is the residual, not a pure-substrate constant — a derivation must produce it from the 3-strand trace normalization, not from data.
